observations: Photo 0 shows a black DSLR camera with a lens attached, resting on white crumpled paper. The camera body has 'Canon' and 'EOS 80D' visible on the front and side. A Canon battery is next to it.

Photo 1 shows the same camera from a top-down angle, with the lens, battery, and a detached screen visible. The lens has markings including '24', '35', '50', '70', '100', '135', indicating a zoom range.
The lens appears to be a Canon EF-S 18-135mm, as the focal length markings match and the lens design is consistent with that model.
The camera body has a visible model label 'EOS 80D' on the front right side in photo 0.
The screen is detached and placed beside the camera in photo 1, suggesting it may be a flip-out screen, which is typical for the 80D.
No signs of major damage are visible in either photo, but close-up shots of the sensor, lens glass, or body dents are missing.

identity.kind: Canon EOS 80D DSLR camera with 18-135mm lens

claims.claim: Canon Eos dslr camera 80d with 18/135mm super zoom lens
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'Canon' and 'EOS 80D' on the camera body. Photo 1 shows lens markings including 18-135mm range.

risks.risk: Lens or sensor damage not visible in photos
risks.proof: Close-up shot of lens glass and camera sensor (requires opening the camera and removing the lens)
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially damaged, reducing value

risks.proof: Video or photo showing battery inserted and camera powering on, screen turning on and responding to touch or buttons
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly non-working, reducing value

risks.risk: Camera body has hidden dents, scratches, or wear not visible in current photos
risks.proof: 360-degree video or close-up photos of all sides of the camera body
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly worn, reducing value

proof_requests: Close-up video or photos of the lens glass and camera sensor (with lens removed)
Video showing the camera powering on with the battery inserted and screen functioning
360-degree photos of the camera body showing all sides for wear or damage
response.reason: The camera model and lens are clearly identifiable from the photos. The seller's claim is supported. Hidden risks exist (sensor, lens, battery, body condition) but are common in used camera sales and can be priced at worst case. The item can be priced based on its worst-case condition as seen.
